---
title: Build a Raycast extension
sidebar_label: Build a Raycast extension
description: Write a small Raycast extension that saves a file from your computer to your instance, with a key of its own that can write files and nothing else.
job: A builder writes a Raycast extension that saves a file to their instance with a key that can write files and nothing else.
kind: tutorial
---

An extension is a client of your instance, like any app you write. It sends requests with a **key**, and the key decides what it may do.

- **You'll build** a Raycast extension with one command, **Save File**. It shows a form where you pick a file, uploads the file and saves it as an item.
- **You need** your own Marfa instance with the CLI signed in, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you, plus [Raycast](https://www.raycast.com) signed in to your Raycast account, which its **Create Extension** command requires, and [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.14 or later.
- **You'll have** a command that saves any file to Marfa, on a key that can write files and nothing else.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Make a key for the extension

Make a key that writes files:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa keys create --label "Raycast" --source raycast --type-permission core.file=write
```

```text
marfa: writing to http://localhost:8600
marfa_k1_…
key 01a1f180-8448-7483-bc7b-658365a3a12f (Raycast); the plaintext is shown once, keep it now
  core.file  Read and Edit
```

</Terminal>

**Copy the line that starts `marfa_k1_` now:** Marfa shows the key once and keeps only a hash of it. If you lose it, make a new one.

`--type-permission` names the one type the key may write, `core.file`, which holds ordinary files. **That also lets it upload bytes:** Marfa takes an upload from a key that may write at least one type. The **source** labels every item the key creates, so you can always tell what the extension saved. [Manage keys](/use/manage-keys) explains each flag, and [Access](/build/access) what a key can hold.

</Step>
<Step>

### Create the extension

Open Raycast and run **Create Extension**. Name it "Marfa Capture", and choose a template and a folder. In the new folder, add the Marfa client:

```bash
npm install @withmarfa/client
```

The [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) is a typed client for every operation, so a mistake in a request fails the type check. In `tsconfig.json`, set `"module": "esnext"` and `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`, so TypeScript finds the client's types.

In `package.json`, replace the template's `commands` with one command, and add two **preferences**, the settings Raycast asks you for. The file's other keys stay as they are:

```json title="package.json"
{
  "commands": [
    { "name": "save-file", "title": "Save File", "description": "Save a file to Marfa", "mode": "view" }
  ],
  "preferences": [
    { "name": "apiUrl", "title": "Server URL", "description": "Where your instance answers, such as http://localhost:8600", "type": "textfield", "required": true },
    { "name": "apiKey", "title": "API Key", "description": "A key made for this extension", "type": "password", "required": true }
  ]
}
```

Raycast runs `src/save-file.tsx` for this command, so delete the template's own command file. It asks for a required preference before the command first runs, and a `password` preference is for secure entry.

</Step>
<Step>

### Keep every call in one module

Put each request in one file, so the rest of the extension never sees a URL or a key. Create `src/marfa.ts` with the client and an error that keeps what the server said:

```ts title="src/marfa.ts"
import { getPreferenceValues } from "@raycast/api";
import { createClient } from "@withmarfa/client";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { basename, extname } from "node:path";

export class MarfaError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: string,
    message: string,
  ) {
    super(message);
  }
}

function client() {
  const { apiUrl, apiKey } = getPreferenceValues<Preferences>();
  return createClient({ baseUrl: apiUrl.trim(), credential: apiKey.trim() });
}

function refused(refusal: { error: { code: string; message: string } }) {
  return new MarfaError(refusal.error.code, refusal.error.message);
}
```

Raycast writes the `Preferences` type from `package.json` into `raycast-env.d.ts` when the extension runs in step 5, so an editor flags `Preferences` until then. Marfa stores bytes under the media type the upload names, so add the types the extension knows. Anything else is stored as plain bytes:

```ts title="src/marfa.ts"
const mediaTypes: Record<string, string> = {
  ".pdf": "application/pdf",
  ".png": "image/png",
  ".jpg": "image/jpeg",
  ".jpeg": "image/jpeg",
  ".txt": "text/plain",
  ".csv": "text/csv",
};
```

Saving a file takes two requests: [upload the bytes](/reference/api/blobs/uploadBlob), then [create an item](/reference/api/items/createItem) that names them:

```ts title="src/marfa.ts"
export async function saveFile(path: string, title: string, notes: string) {
  const marfa = client();
  const upload = await marfa.POST("/blobs", {
    body: await readFile(path),
    headers: { "Content-Type": mediaTypes[extname(path).toLowerCase()] ?? "application/octet-stream" },
  });
  if (upload.error) throw refused(upload.error);
  const { hash, mime_type } = upload.data;

  const properties: Record<string, unknown> = { blob_ref: hash, mime_type, title: title || basename(path) };
  if (notes) properties.notes = notes;
  const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/items", { body: { type: "core.file", properties } });
  if (error) throw refused(error);
  return data.item;
}
```

The upload answers the bytes' `hash` and the `mime_type` Marfa stores them under, which is the type of the first upload of the same bytes. A file item requires both. Each call returns `data` when it works and `error` when Marfa refuses, with a stable `code`. [Files](/build/files) explains how a blob and its item fit together.

</Step>
<Step>

### Build the form

Create `src/save-file.tsx`. It saves the chosen file and shows the outcome in a toast, Raycast's short message:

```tsx title="src/save-file.tsx"
import { Action, ActionPanel, Form, popToRoot, showToast, Toast } from "@raycast/api";
import { MarfaError, saveFile } from "./marfa";

type Values = { files: string[]; title: string; notes: string };

async function save(values: Values) {
  const [path] = values.files;
  if (!path) {
    await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Failure, title: "Choose a file first" });
    return;
  }
  const toast = await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Animated, title: "Uploading" });
  try {
    const item = await saveFile(path, values.title.trim(), values.notes.trim());
    toast.style = Toast.Style.Success;
    toast.title = "Saved";
    toast.message = item.id;
    await popToRoot();
  } catch (error) {
    toast.style = Toast.Style.Failure;
    toast.title = error instanceof MarfaError ? `Refused: ${error.code}` : "Could not save the file";
    toast.message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
  }
}
```

Add the form that calls it:

```tsx title="src/save-file.tsx"
export default function SaveFile() {
  return (
    <Form
      actions={
        <ActionPanel>
          <Action.SubmitForm title="Save to Marfa" onSubmit={save} />
        </ActionPanel>
      }
    >
      <Form.FilePicker id="files" title="File" allowMultipleSelection={false} />
      <Form.TextField id="title" title="Title" placeholder="The file's name" />
      <Form.TextArea id="notes" title="Notes" />
    </Form>
  );
}
```

Each control's `id` names the value it fills. A file picker's value is a list of paths, even for one file. The item takes the key's `source`, `raycast`. [File](/catalog/file) lists every field the type holds.

</Step>
<Step>

### Run the extension

In the extension's folder, start development mode:

```bash
npm run dev
```

It adds the extension to the top of Raycast's root search, and it writes `raycast-env.d.ts`. In a second terminal in the same folder, check the types:

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
```

`tsc` prints nothing when the types are right.

Search for **Save File**. Raycast asks for the preferences first: enter your instance's address, such as `http://localhost:8600`, and paste the key from step 1. Choose a file and run **Save to Marfa**. A **Saved** toast shows the new item's ID. Check it from the CLI:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa items list --source raycast
```

```text
id                                    type       when                      title
01a1f181-edb3-75e6-8405-b7a0178c4cef  core.file  2026-11-19T01:53:06.483Z  kitchen-plan.txt
```

</Terminal>

`marfa items get` with that ID shows the `blob_ref`, `mime_type` and `size_bytes`. Stop `npm run dev` with Control-C when you're done: the extension stays in Raycast.
